title: JOLTS Job Openings (Sep 2026)
source: BLS: bls.gov/schedule/news_release/jolts.htm, re-fetched direct 2026-09-05 — the series schedule reads verbatim 'September 2026 | Nov. 03, 2026 | 10:00 AM', corroborated by bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched_list.htm ('Tuesday, November 3, 2026, 10:00 AM: Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for September 2026'), which carries JOLTS exactly once in the month. No contradicting view found. Promoted estimate -> confirmed by this event's own initial-research session (2026-09-05), which is the promotion the filing entry deferred to it: the discovering lane (the jolts-2026-12-01 sweep) may not self-confirm an adjacency it found in-sweep, and the confirming re-read it named was this same jolts.htm schedule page. Reference-month-end to release lag across the schedule's thirteen listed rows runs 29-41 days; this print is 34, i.e. the ordinary cadence
notes: CLOSES AN OPEN ITEM THE SERIES BANKED RATHER THAN GUESSED. The jolts-2026-09-29 pulse of 2026-08-30 identified this exact release as missing from the calendar and deliberately did NOT file it: 'no source-published date was found — BLS's November schedule is not posted and every result was an extrapolation. Proposing a guessed date would manufacture the very thing the EST:/NEWS: prefixes exist to prevent; recorded as an open item for the next pulse instead.' The schedule is posted now, so the item is filed on a primary rather than an extrapolation. THREE THINGS MAKE THIS INSTANCE UNUSUAL. (1) It lands on MIDTERM ELECTION DAY — midterm-elections-2026-11-03 (high impact) — so a medium-impact 10:00 ET slack read publishes into a session whose tape is about something else entirely; expect no attributable footprint. (2) It is the first labor read after fomc-2026-10-28 (the no-SEP meeting) and the last JOLTS before jolts-2026-12-01 and the fomc-2026-12-09 SEP/dot-plot meeting. (3) It is the release MOST exposed to a 2026-10-01 funding lapse: its reference month is September and it publishes ~33 days after government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 (estimate). The 2025 precedent, read off the JOLTS schedule page's own scar, is that this is the slot a lapse consumes — that page carries no Sep-2025 row and resumes at 'October 2025 | Dec. 09, 2025', while the BLS API still carries 2025-M09 openings of 7,169k, i.e. the data survived and the standalone release did not. Proposed during the jolts-2026-12-01 initial research (2026-09-05). DATE RISK, NOW SOURCED RATHER THAN INFERRED (initial research, 2026-09-05): bls.gov/bls/2025-lapse-revised-release-dates.htm (last modified 2026-02-12) carries the September-2025 JOLTS, originally Tuesday November 4 2025, as 'Canceled (see JOLTS note)', with October-2025 data slipped Dec 2 -> Dec 9; USDL-25-1555 states the mechanism verbatim ('Publication of the September 2025 JOLTS news release was canceled due to a lapse in appropriations') and attaches a partial-collection data-quality caveat to that month. The same page shows the SHORT early-2026 lapse costing JOLTS only two days (December-2025 data, Feb 3 -> Feb 5). Nov 4 2025 and Nov 3 2026 are the same slot one year apart - same September reference month, same Tuesday, same ~5-week lag - so the exposure this entry flagged is exact, and it grades by lapse DURATION rather than by a lapse occurring. The data itself survives either way: the BLS API carries 2025-M09 openings of 7,169k. A CONFIRMED date is not immunity; re-verify at the first pulse after government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 resolves.
